title: ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY
summary: Purchase order validation error raised by po_save when an order line tax code does not match the supplier country.

infobox.message: TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)

body:
`ERR-PO-0412` is a validation error raised by the Ledgerline purchase order module when an order line tax code does not match the supplier account's recorded country [^r1][^r4][^r18]. It occurs primarily because the system's fetch action automatically populates the domestic UK tax code on purchase orders, even for non-UK vendors [^r5][^r8][^r19]. Saving an overseas order without manually adjusting the line tax code to a reverse-charge code triggers this error and blocks the transaction [^r2][^r7][^r12].

## Meaning

The error displays the message `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)`, where the country code appended in brackets reflects the country recorded on the supplier account [^r1][^r14][^r18]. It signals that an incorrect tax code was selected on a purchase order line [^r17]. The message appears in the system status bar, in error dialogs, and within background batch processing logs [^r16].

## Cause

`ERR-PO-0412` occurs on [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] when saving an order for an overseas supplier whose line tax code retains the default domestic entry rather than a reverse-charge code [^r2][^r7]. Ledgerline's Fetch function automatically defaults `VAT20-UK` on purchase order lines, regardless of whether a vendor is based in an overseas country such as the Netherlands or Poland [^r5][^r8][^r10][^r19]. UK suppliers require a `-UK` tax code, while suppliers located in any other country require an equivalent reverse-charge `-RC` code [^r4]. Frequent occurrences indicate that an overseas supplier profile was configured with domestic defaults [^r23].

## How to fix

To resolve the error, users must verify the supplier country on the record and amend the line tax code to match the supplier's location [^r3][^r15]. For suppliers outside the UK, change the tax code to `VAT20-RC` for standard goods or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items [^r9][^r20]. For a UK-registered supplier, the tax code must be set to `VAT20-UK` [^r21]. After updating the tax code, keep the cursor in the line details area and press F8 to save and recommit the order [^r3][^r22]. 

Users must never force a purchase order through using domestic tax codes for an overseas supplier account, as doing so distorts tax returns [^r24]. If the error recurs frequently for a specific vendor, notify the purchase ledger team to review and correct the supplier master profile [^r23].

## Raised by

The error is raised by the `po_save` service within [[services-pur-po]] during order validation against the vendor address record [^r6][^r11][^r13][^r15]. It triggers when the tax code entered on the order fails to match the supplier country state returned by `po_fetch` [^r11][^r12][^r13].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Message text change (current vs. superseded)**: Today, following patch 7.2.3-P1, the error text is `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)` [^r1][^r14]. Older documentation and legacy Ledgerline 7.0 system manuals phrased the message as `TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE` [^r14][^r25][^r27].
* **Resolution terminology (current vs. superseded)**: Under [[sop-pur-002|SOP-PUR-002]] v1.4, the remedy requires updating the line tax code to reverse-charge codes like `VAT20-RC` on PUR-PO-01 [^r2][^r3]. The superseded SOP-PUR-002 v1.3 and Ledgerline 7.0 manual described this as correcting regional authority assignments or updating master records [^r26][^r27][^r28].

## See also

* [[errors-po|ERR-PO Error Codes]]
* [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01 Purchase Order Entry]]
* [[services-pur-po|PUR po services]]
* [[sop-pur-002|SOP-PUR-002 Purchase Request to Purchase Order]]
* [[data-tax-codes|Tax codes]]

r1.loc_text: sheet Error codes, row ERR-PO-0412, SHEET Error codes
r1.quote: code=ERR-PO-0412 | message=TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>) | module=PO

r2.quote: For a supplier outside the UK change it to VAT20-RC, or Save fails with ERR-PO-0412.

r3.section: What to do when something does not look right
r3.loc_text: p. 4, What to do when something does not look right
r3.quote: Where the vendor is located outside the UK, amend the line tax code from VAT20-UK to VAT20-RC and press F8 again.

r4.file: 03_ledgerline_manuals/MAN-ERR-72 Message and Error Code Reference v7.2.3.pdf
r4.quote: Cause: the tax code is for the wrong country. A UK supplier needs a -UK code; a supplier in any other country needs a reverse-charge -RC code.

r5.file: 03_ledgerline_manuals/MAN-ERR-72 Message and Error Code Reference v7.2.3.pdf
r5.quote: Fetch always fills VAT20-UK. Remedy: change the tax code to the -RC code with the same rate (for example VAT20-RC) and save again.

r6.file: 03_ledgerline_manuals/MAN-ERR-72 Message and Error Code Reference v7.2.3.pdf

r7.quote: For a supplier in another country you must change it to the reverse-charge code (-RC) before saving; otherwise Save fails with ERR-PO-0412.

r8.section: 17.2 ERR-PO-0412 Tax code does not match supplier country
r8.loc_text: p. 10, §17.2 ERR-PO-0412 Tax code does not match supplier country
r8.quote: Cause: the tax code is for the wrong country. A UK supplier needs a -UK code; a supplier in any other country needs a reverse-charge -RC code. Fetch always fills VAT20-UK.

r9.section: 17.2 ERR-PO-0412 Tax code does not match supplier country
r9.loc_text: p. 10, §17.2 ERR-PO-0412 Tax code does not match supplier country
r9.quote: Remedy: change the tax code to the -RC code with the same rate (for example VAT20-RC) and save again.

r10.quote: Fetch defaults the tax code to the plant's state; an overseas supplier needs the -RC code ERR-PO-0412

r11.quote: ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)

r12.quote: tax_cd is always returned as VAT20-UK, whatever the supplier's country. An overseas supplier needs VAT20-RC on po_save (ERR-PO-0412).

r13.quote: {code: ERR-PO-0412, msg: "TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)"}

r14.quote: The text of ERR-PO-0412 changes from TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE to TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY, with the supplier's country code in brackets.

r15.quote: The existing rule continues to ensure that the chosen tax code corresponds correctly to the location recorded on the master record for the supplier.

r16.quote: The same updated wording will appear in the system status bar, in error dialogs, and within the background process logs when orders are processed by batch jobs.

r18.quote: Read the code: ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (NL).

r19.quote: Fetch always fills VAT20-UK, the code for a UK supplier, even when the supplier is in the Netherlands or Poland.

r20.quote: Supplier outside the UK: change the tax code to VAT20-RC (or VAT5-RC for reduced-rate items).

r21.quote: If the supplier is registered in the UK, select VAT20-UK instead.

r22.quote: Ensure the cursor remains in the line details area while pressing the key so the validation routine runs against the amended field.

r23.quote: If you regularly raise orders for the same overseas vendor and the error persists on fresh orders, notify the purchase ledger team

r24.quote: Never force an order through using domestic tax codes for an overseas account, as this distorts the tax returns.

r25.quote: ERR-PO-0412 TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE Change the tax region on the order to the supplier's state.

r26.quote: For a supplier outside the UK change it to VAT20-RC, or Save fails with ERR-PO-0412.

r27.quote: The message is triggered during purchase order entry whenever the tax code applied to an individual line or the order header points to a regional authority that disagrees with the master record

r28.quote: The tax code's region is not the supplier's state. Change the tax code.
